steps.title: Prepare all required stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make the following solutions using Milli‑Q water unless stated otherwise: (a) Mobile phase for TLC – mix 10 ml water, 1 ml 36 % ammonium hydroxide, 48 ml methanol, then add 88 ml chloroform slowly; store in a brown glass bottle. (b) Undecaprenol and undecaprenyl‑monophosphate diammonium salt – dissolve each to 1 mM in chloroform‑methanol (2:1, v/v) and store in brown glass vials at –20 °C. (c) 6 M pyridinium acetate – mix 51.5 ml glacial acetic acid with 48.5 ml pyridine. (d) n‑Butanol/pyridinium acetate pH 4.2 – mix 50 ml n‑butanol with 25 ml 6 M pyridinium acetate. (e) HEPES/KOH stock (1 M, pH 7.5) – dissolve 23.83 g HEPES in 90 ml water, adjust pH to 7.5 with 1 M KOH, bring to 100 ml. (f) HEPES/NaOH stock (1 M, pH 7.5) – dissolve 23.83 g HEPES in 90 ml water, adjust pH to 7.5 with 1 M NaOH, bring to 100 ml. (g) Sodium phosphate buffer (80 mM, pH 4.8) – dissolve 0.64 g NaOH in 150 ml water, adjust pH to 4.8 with 85 % phosphoric acid, bring to 200 ml. (h) Muramidase cellosyl (0.5 µg µl⁻¹) – dissolve 5 mg freeze‑dried cellosyl in 10 ml 20 mM sodium phosphate pH 4.8, aliquot and store at –20 °C. (i) Sodium borate (0.5 M, pH 9.0) – dissolve 3.09 g boric acid in 75 ml water, adjust to pH 9.0 with 10 M NaOH, bring to 100 ml. (j) HPLC buffer A – dissolve 4 g NaOH (HPLC grade) in 1 900 ml water, adjust to pH 4.31 with 85 % phosphoric acid, bring to 2 L, filter 0.22 µm, add 20 µl 10 % sodium azide per L. (k) HPLC buffer B – dissolve 6 g NaOH (HPLC grade) in 1 500 ml water, adjust to pH 4.95 with 85 % phosphoric acid, bring to 1.7 L, filter 0.22 µm, add 300 ml methanol.

steps.title: Prepare Lys‑type lipid II assay
steps.instruction: In a 1.5 ml microtube add lipid II (40 µM final) together with 30 mM HEPES/KOH pH 7.5, 150 mM KCl, 0.1 % (w/v) Triton X‑100 to a total volume of 50 µl. Add 2 µM phosphatase (e.g., TelCt), phosphatase‑inhibitor complex (e.g., TelCt‑TipC) or no enzyme for a control. Incubate 90 min at 37 °C in a shaking incubator set to 800 rpm.

steps.title: Prepare undecaprenyl monophosphate assay
steps.instruction: In a 1.5 ml microtube combine 100 µM undecaprenyl monophosphate with 20 mM HEPES/KOH pH 7.5, 150 mM KCl, 1 mM CaCl₂, 0.1 % Triton X‑100 to 50 µl total. Add 2 µM phosphatase or no enzyme (control). Incubate 90 min at 37 °C, 800 rpm.

steps.title: Prepare undecaprenyl pyrophosphate synthesis assay
steps.instruction: In a 1.5 ml microtube assemble a reaction containing 40 µM farnesyl pyrophosphate, 400 µM isopentenyl pyrophosphate, 10 µM UppS, 20 mM HEPES/KOH pH 7.5, 50 mM KCl, 0.5 mM MgCl₂, 1 mM CaCl₂, 0.1 % Triton X‑100 to a final volume of 50 µl. Add 2 µM phosphatase, phosphatase‑inhibitor complex, or no enzyme. Incubate 5 h at 25 °C, then an additional 90 min at 37 °C, shaking at 800 rpm.

steps.title: Prepare undecaprenol assay
steps.instruction: In a 1.5 ml microtube mix 100 µM undecaprenol with 30 mM HEPES/KOH pH 7.5, 150 mM KCl, 0.1 % Triton X‑100 to 50 µl total. Incubate 90 min at 37 °C, 800 rpm.

steps.title: Terminate reactions and extract organic phase
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl n‑butanol/pyridine acetate (2:1) pH 4.2 to each 50 µl reaction. Vortex 1 min, then centrifuge 3 min at 17 000 × g using a bench‑top centrifuge. Collect the upper organic (n‑butanol) phase, which represents ~1/3 of the total volume.

steps.title: Perform thin‑layer chromatography
steps.instruction: All TLC steps are done in a fume hood at room temperature unless otherwise noted. (1) Prepare the developing chamber: pour the mobile phase (10 ml water, 1 ml 36 % NH₄OH, 48 ml methanol, 88 ml chloroform), set solvent level to 1 cm, close lid and let the chamber saturate for 60 min. (2) Pre‑heat the HPTLC silica gel plate for 1 h at 60 °C to remove humidity. (3) Using a pencil draw a line 1.5 cm from the bottom; mark sample spots 2 cm apart, keeping at least 4 cm from the plate edges. (4) Load the organic phase: pipette 10 µl onto each spot, dry each spot with a heat gun (or under the hood) being careful not to transfer any aqueous phase. (5) Develop the plate: place it in the chamber so the solvent level is 0.5 cm below the pencil line; run until the solvent front reaches 4/5 of the plate length (≈1.5–2 h). (6) Remove plate, dry with a heat gun until completely dry. (7) Stain: place a small beaker with solid iodine in the chamber, close lid and let the chamber saturate for 20–30 min at room temperature; then expose the dried plate to iodine vapor until spots are clearly visible (20 min–1 h).

steps.title: Prepare radiolabeled lipid II for HPLC
steps.instruction: Dry 10 000 dpm (~1 nmol) [¹⁴C]GlcNAc‑labeled lipid II‑Lys (stored in chloroform/methanol 1:1) in a glass vial under vacuum. Resuspend the dried lipid II in 5 µl 0.2 % (w/v) Triton X‑100 and vortex 10 s at 1 800 rpm.

steps.title: Set up HPLC reaction mixtures
steps.instruction: In a 1.5 ml microtube prepare 100 µl reaction buffer containing 15 mM HEPES/NaOH pH 7.5, 10 mM MgCl₂, 150 mM NaCl, 0.023 % Triton X‑100 and 0.4 mM CaCl₂ (omit CaCl₂ for the PBP1B‑LpoB control). Add either 2 µM phosphatase (TelCt or Colicin M), phosphatase‑inhibitor complex (TelCt‑TipC), or for the control add 0.75 µM PBP1B and 1.5 µM LpoB. Mix the reaction buffer with the resuspended lipid II and incubate 60 min at 37 °C, 800 rpm. Spin down any condensation in a microcentrifuge.

steps.title: Process phosphatase reaction samples for HPLC
steps.instruction: For reactions containing phosphatase (or its inhibitor complex): adjust the sample pH to 3.5–4.0 by adding 20 % phosphoric acid (measure pH with 0.3 µl on a pH‑indicator strip). Centrifuge 15 min at maximum speed at room temperature. Transfer the clear supernatant into an HPLC vial equipped with a 400 µl glass insert.

steps.title: Process PBP1B‑LpoB control samples
steps.instruction: After the initial 60 min incubation, heat the sample 5 min at 100 °C in a dry bath, then centrifuge to remove condensation and cool 2 min at room temperature. Add 30 µl cellosyl buffer (80 mM sodium phosphate, pH 4.8) and 10 µl 0.5 µg µl⁻¹ cellosyl (or mutanolysin). Incubate 70 min at 37 °C, 800 rpm, then centrifuge. Boil the reaction 10 min at 100 °C, centrifuge 15 min at maximum speed, RT. Prepare a new 2 ml microcentrifuge tube with a small hole in the lid (puncture with a needle) to release H₂ gas. Transfer the supernatant into this tube. Reduce muropeptides by adding 100 µl 0.5 M sodium borate pH 9.0 and ~1 mg solid sodium borohydride. Incubate 30 min at room temperature while spinning at 4 700 × g to prevent spillage. Adjust pH again to 3.5–4.0 with 20 % phosphoric acid (measure with 0.3 µl on a strip). Centrifuge 15 min at maximum speed, RT, and transfer the supernatant into an HPLC vial with a 400 µl insert.

steps.title: Set up and run HPLC analysis
steps.instruction: Configure the HPLC system with a C18 reversed‑phase column, flow rate 0.5 ml min⁻¹, column temperature 55 °C, and a radioactivity flow‑through detector. (1) Wash column with 100 % methanol for 20 min at room temperature. (2) Start a linear gradient for 30 min from 100 % methanol to 100 % Milli‑Q water, then hold 100 % water for 20 min. (3) Wash with HPLC buffer B for 20 min and equilibrate with buffer A for 40 min. (4) Run a blank buffer run using the same gradient without injecting a sample. (5) Inject each sample: leave 20 µl of the reaction volume in the 400 µl vial insert, flush the injection loop with buffer A for 2 min, then start a linear elution gradient for 60 min from 100 % buffer A to 50 % buffer B, hold 50 % buffer B for 10 min. (6) Re‑equilibrate the column with 100 % buffer A for 30 min before the next injection.
